scope: Only generated images and 2D screening; no 3D reconstruction, old model modifications or 3D relighting.

requests.name: approach
requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit, controlled viewpoint continuation.
Image 1 is the canonical original AI canal photograph. Image 2 is a previous small right-shift viewpoint candidate of that same scene, only auxiliary reference. Original image 1 wins if details disagree.
Generate ONE actual next-view photograph for a camera WALKING TOWARD THE RED-AWNING CAFE entrance from the original street viewpoint. Do not redesign any architecture. This is a near-doorway examination image for checking future 3D reconstruction, not an artistic reinterpretation.

Keep exact identity and topology: cream stucco left building; burgundy red awning with black circular hanging sign; warm dark wooden storefront, original division into the left glazed bay, central narrow door and right glazed bay; identical upper shutters and window placement wherever visible. The teal bookstore remains adjacent on the right, and then the olive shop. Bicycles and round cafe table with chairs stay in the same sidewalk positions.
Camera: move forward along the left-bank pavement and toward this cafe's original central doorway, eye level, normal perspective lens. Stand about half a metre outside its threshold, aiming into the room at a gentle oblique angle, showing enough of the original awning and wooden window/door framing to identify the SAME cafe. The original canal and arched bridge may appear only as a peripheral sliver if physically visible; do not compress the whole wide exterior into this close-up.
Open the original central door inward about 65 degrees on a plausible existing hinge, keeping its width, frame and panel design. Keep neighbouring panes and wall positions fixed.
Interior continuity: the original photograph already shows warm wood shelving, products, cups, pendant lamps and a cafe-like service interior through the windows. Maintain that visible arrangement and warm wood/brass palette. Extend only newly exposed floor, wall and cabinet surfaces into a plausible coherent room. Do not replace the photographed interior with a generic teal-wainscot empty room. No invented second entrance, extra windows, new furniture blocking the doorway, or extra shop. Keep one continuous floor and physically plausible door swing clearance.
Same dusk, warm interior lights on, same wet paving, material textures and exposure character. Glass has plausible transmission and restrained reflections; interior shelves should be actual solid objects in the depiction, not a flat scene pasted on the glazing.
One clean photorealistic landscape 16:9 image, no text or diagrams.

requests.name: interior-on-v1-threshold
requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / rigid interior viewpoint continuation.
Image 1: the authoritative canonical original canal exterior.
Image 2: the immediately previous generated NEAR-DOORWAY view of that SAME red-awning cafe. Preserve the architectural details, visible interior, door, lamps and fixtures in image 2 as the continuity reference.
Generate ONE photorealistic next camera photograph after stepping THROUGH THAT OPEN DOOR into the SAME cafe. Do not redesign it or make a generic cafe.

Camera: eye-level, just inside the threshold, about 1.0 to 1.5 metres into the room; aim diagonally toward the service counter on the interior-left side and the rear shelving. Use a natural wide lens around 28-32mm full-frame equivalent, straight verticals, no fisheye. The shopfront is behind the camera. A little edge of its dark wooden jamb may appear at a far edge, but do not put the canal, bridge or a second storefront on the back wall.
Keep a single plausible rectangular interior: entering from the street facing the back, a wood-and-brass counter occupies the LEFT portion; the existing shelves of ceramic jars, cups, glass containers, pastries and warm woodwork remain on and behind this counter. An aisle extends toward the back. Only a small amount of seating is on the RIGHT side; it must not obstruct the door or counter. Retain the cream plaster, dark timber ceiling beams, wood parquet floor and the SAME brass hanging lamps visible in the doorway reference. Infer newly revealed backs and side surfaces as contiguous objects, not flat photos on walls. Do not add a second entrance, stairs, a new room, extra exterior windows, different furniture style, neon signage, teal paneling or people.
The actual doorway view already establishes the front window bays, center inward-opening door, wooden counter with glass pastry domes and white cups, shelves and interior pendants. These are ONE fixed scene: preserve object shapes, positions, materials and pendant styles when changing camera location. The degree of the open door and all exterior conditions stay unchanged.
Same dusk lighting with the cafe's interior electric lights ON. Plausible warm light falloff, contact shadows, glass transmission and restrained reflections. High photographic fidelity matching the input, no video motion blur, no labels, collage, text or overlays. Single landscape 16:9 image.

requests.name: interior-on
requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit, single camera-location correction.
Image 1 is the just-generated cafe interior continuity reference and edit target. Image 2 is the prior exterior doorway reference to identify the same shop.
Change ONLY the camera position: it has now walked 1.5 metres forward beyond the entrance threshold into the centre of the existing aisle, and looks diagonally left toward the same long wood service counter and rear shelves. The entrance door and both front window jambs are now BEHIND the camera and entirely out of frame. This is not a photo taken through a doorway: no dark vertical doorframe borders, no door handle at the image edge, no foreground glazing covering the view.
Keep the same fixed room and furnishings from image 1: the long left wood-and-stone counter with pastry domes and white cup stacks, the espresso machine farther along it, the wall-mounted wood shelves and jars, the back shelving on the rear wall, the same tables/chairs to the right, the same timber beam ceiling, cream plaster and wood parquet. All objects stay in the SAME world positions. Near objects may exit the frame due to camera translation, but do not move them deeper into the room to keep them visible. Show the new occlusion and parallax expected from stepping further inside.
Keep the same warm electric lights on and same dusk, exposure character, materials and photographic style. Retain distinctive fixture shapes and the number/positions of pendant lamps that remain visible; do not invent new doors, exterior windows, service counters, plants or aisles. The existing room continues behind the near camera position.
Single clean photorealistic landscape 16:9 image, no diagram, text, collage, border or arrows.

requests.name: interior-off
requests.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather, same-camera lights-off counterfactual.
The supplied image is the EDIT TARGET: the SAME cafe interior photograph, viewed from inside the front of the room. Produce an otherwise identical frame with the cafe's artificial illumination switched OFF.

CHANGE ONLY LIGHT EMISSION AND ITS PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCES:
All existing brass pendant lamps remain physically in the identical locations and shapes but their bulbs are dark. All interior wall sconces are off. Extinguish the small tabletop candle/votive lights and turn off espresso-machine indicator illumination. Remove the warm pools of light, warm ceiling/wall glow and lamp reflections on the stone counter, pastry domes, glass jars and floor that these light sources caused.
The time remains the SAME blue-hour dusk. The only remaining light is faint, cool outdoor sky/street illumination entering from the ORIGINAL entrance/windows behind the camera; rear shelves should become much dimmer than front objects. No sunlight, new windows, new fill lights, night-vision look, artificial brightening or automatic exposure compensation. Keep camera exposure / white balance / framing unchanged. Preserve real wood/material colors where still lit, rather than applying a uniform blue filter or just lowering global image brightness. Glossy highlights should respond to the remaining illumination.

PIXEL GEOMETRY AND OBJECT IDENTITY MUST STAY FIXED:
Do not move the camera, crop, zoom, change the lens, move furniture, change perspective, redraw the room layout, change beam or shelving positions, alter door/window counts, add/remove any jars or cups, relocate pastries or flowers, or change chairs/table/counter shapes.
Keep the foreground pastry domes, large flower vase, espresso machine, brass service bell, cup stacks, right round table with pink flowers, all back-wall shelves and all ceiling beams in EXACTLY the same projected positions as the input. All pendant fixtures must still exist unlit; do not erase them.
Single photorealistic landscape image, identical composition and aspect ratio, no labels, borders or collage.

requests.name: reverse
requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / reverse camera consistency test.
Image 1 is the current LIGHTS-ON cafe interior, canonical for room geometry, furnishings and camera location.
Image 2 is the immediately previous exterior approach view, canonical for the front door/window arrangement and open door.
Image 3 is the original canal scene, canonical for the outdoor environment and its relationship to the cafe.
Generate ONE photorealistic photograph from the SAME inside location as image 1, with the camera turned about 180 degrees toward the ORIGINAL FRONT DOOR AND STREET. Do not move to another room or redesign the room.

RIGID ROOM CONTINUITY:
The long service counter that was to the camera's LEFT when looking into the shop must now appear to its RIGHT when facing back out. Keep the same wood/stone counter, pastry domes, large white flower arrangement, cup stacks and espresso machine at their established positions; only the visible sides and occlusion change. The seating that was on the interior RIGHT should now be on the camera LEFT. Keep the same brass pendants and timber beam ceiling. The rear-wall shelves from image 1 are now behind the camera and should NOT become the front wall.
Show the SAME single narrow centre entrance and its flanking wooden glazed bays established in image 2, seen from INSIDE. From inside looking out, the original door's hinge is on the LEFT, and the leaf remains opened inward at the same angle. Do not invent a wide double door, additional front entrances, extra windows or a different storefront. The burgundy-red awning can be glimpsed above the exterior glazing, consistently attached outside.

OUTDOOR CONTINUITY:
Beyond that entrance is the same wet left-bank pavement and the canal; the dusk sky and street lamps retain the same lighting. The stone arched bridge is farther along the bank in the direction of the adjacent teal and olive shops. From this reversed indoor direction, that direction is to the LEFT; if the bridge is visible it belongs on the left part of the outdoor view, not as a huge centred arch pasted onto the doorway. Do NOT copy the cafe/teal/olive storefront row onto the opposite bank. Those shops are neighbours on the SAME front-wall plane and are mostly outside this reverse view. Only show the canal, far-bank scenery and the limited street surfaces actually visible through the existing openings. The original exterior table/chairs and bicycles remain outside beside the facade; they must not appear as duplicate indoor props.
The nearby counter and front wall should correctly occlude parts of the outside. Reflections on front glazing can show interior lamps but must not replace the outside with a flat panorama.
Lighting: same electric lights ON inside, blue-hour dusk outside, natural exposure balance showing both without an impossibly bright outdoor day scene.
Single natural wide-lens 16:9 photograph, straight verticals, no text, diagrams, collage or frame.
